reason: Six verified lifecycle defects in the API and storage layer. (1) DELETE /chat-sessions/{id} only called store.delete_chat_session, which never listed harness_sessions among a conversation's owned records and never called harness_runtime.close_session, so deleting a Claude/Codex chat left the vendor process and MCP gateway alive in the runtime until Core restarted and the orphaned HarnessSession row kept engagement_has_dependents refusing project deletion. The route now closes the vendor session first (HarnessStateError for an active turn is still a 409) unless a mission continued from the chat still references it, and delete_chat_session cascades the conversation's harness_sessions rows by id with the same run-sharing guard. (2) ApiEntityValidator.validate_delete paginated every kind through list_entities on the event loop, so one corrupt row of any kind made every generic DELETE a 500; it now runs under asyncio.to_thread and iterates NebulaStore.iter_readable_entities, which skips and records rows that fail validation. (3) Knowledge and Library ingest routes returned 503 'retry or reindex' after the KnowledgeSource/LibraryItem and Artifact rows were already committed in error status, so each retry created another error-state source; ingest_document/ingest_library_item now raise KnowledgeSourceIndexError/LibraryItemIndexError carrying the recorded row and the routes return it as 201 with status 'error' plus a degraded diagnostic, so the client reindexes by id. (4) exporter._all_entities omitted temporary 'Ask Nebula' sessions (list_entities hides temporary_assistant unless include_temporary) while exporting their messages, turns and snapshots; it now passes include_temporary=True. (5) pending_pairings was only ever popped on a successful redeem, so abandoned pairings grew for the process lifetime; prune_expired_pairings now drops expired offers on every create and redeem. (6) The execution, run and browser-assessment event websockets polled the database every 250 ms forever with no terminal frame; after the owning record reaches a terminal status and one more poll drains nothing they send {kind: complete} and close with 1000, which both UI stream clients already treat as closed. Tests: test_storage::test_delete_chat_session_removes_its_harness_session_unless_a_mission_shares_it and test_chat_api::test_deleting_a_harness_chat_closes_its_vendor_session (harness row survived / 204 instead of 409 on main), test_api::test_generic_delete_skips_unreadable_rows_of_unrelated_kinds (500 on main), test_knowledge::test_ingest_returns_the_recorded_source_when_the_index_write_fails (503 on main), test_exporter::test_export_includes_temporary_assistant_sessions_with_their_messages (no chat_sessions in the bundle on main), test_chat_api::test_expired_pairings_are_pruned_when_pairings_are_created_or_redeemed (no pruning on main), test_api::test_run_event_websocket_completes_and_closes_after_a_terminal_run (heartbeat instead of complete on main). test_temporary_chat and test_knowledge_index cover the popup discard sequence and the Chroma-backed ingest paths that share the changed code.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change (the complete frame is ignored by parseEventFrame and a 1000 close is already treated as closed in events.ts and assessmentEvents.ts). No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (the real-Core journey suite matched through api.py and storage.py) does not delete harness chats, corrupt rows, break the knowledge index, export bundles, expire pairings or watch a finished mission socket to its close; the Python tests drive each of these directly. No full suites.
